title: Attachment and Duty
body:
Attachment and Duty

With the failure of the peace mission, Kunti was overwhelmed with grief, realising that a war of absolute destruction was now unavoidable. Tormented by the thought that her first-born son, Karna, would stand on the opposite side of the battlefield against his own brothers, she decided to seek him out and reveal the secret of his birth to save both him and the Pandavas.
She went to the banks of the Yamuna where Karna was performing his daily prayers. Standing silently behind him, she shielded his back from the burning rays of the sun with the hem of her upper garment. When Karna finished his meditations, he turned and bowed respectfully to the queen of Hastinapura, expressing his amazement at her presence. Kunti revealed the truth of his birth: that he was Surya's first-born son, born of her womb before her marriage, and urged him to join his brothers and be crowned as the rightful emperor of the realm.
Karna felt a quiet warmth in his heart, sensing that the Sun god endorsed Kunti's request. However, with an extraordinary effort of will, he controlled his emotions and refused her plea. He sadly but firmly pointed out that she had abandoned him as a helpless babe, depriving him of his birthright, and that Duryodhana had given him love, trust, and a kingdom when he was rejected by all. He argued that deserting Duryodhana on the eve of the battle would be black treachery and base ingratitude, unworthy of a true kshatriya.
However, Karna promised that her plea would not be entirely in vain. He vowed that he would spare the lives of four of her sons—Yudhishthira, Bhima, Nakula, and Sahadeva—regardless of what they did to him. He would target only Arjuna, ensuring that whether he fell or Arjuna died, Kunti would still have five sons. Overwhelmed by his noble adherence to the kshatriya code, Kunti embraced him in silence, resigning herself to the inexorable workings of destiny.
